answer_raw:
The **buzz cut** is your best balance of style and low maintenance.

**Shaving it** is the lowest maintenance option and offers a sharp, decisive look, but it requires regular scalp maintenance and can be a much more radical change than a buzz [6]. If you have a patchy hairline, a bald look or a very close buzz can feel more controlled [6].

**Buzz cutting** is a great first step because it leaves some texture to soften the transition [6]. You can use a #1 guard to leave about 1/8 inch of hair, which covers scars or bumps while still looking very short [8]. Choosing a #1 guard is also a good option if your scalp is sensitive [8].

**Keeping the sides** while shaving the rest—commonly known as an undercut or shaved sides—creates a sharp contrast between the short sides and longer top [2][7]. An undercut can be striking with thick hair but often requires more styling (like gels or pomades) to manage the volume on top [7]. If you go this route, a skin fade provides a softer, more seamless blend than a hard line [8].
